final.title: Check data residency before you automate
final.body:
Before you automate a workflow, make data residency the first control, not a footnote. By residency, I mean where the data is allowed to live and move: in your own systems, in a specific country, or inside a vendor service. For an owner-operator, the real question is not “can AI do this?” but “which parts of this one workflow are allowed to leave my environment at all?”

Take one recurring task you already do by hand, such as customer-data entry, invoice processing, or lead follow-up. Treat it as an example, not a customer case. Then list the fields that you would not want to hand to a third party: payment details, personal data, internal pricing, or anything a supplier agreement keeps in place. That is the bounded decision. AI can sit on top of a workflow, but the data path still needs to make sense.

Next, check the tool’s own service terms and data-handling docs. Don’t rely on the demo. If the vendor cannot keep those fields where you need them, the workflow is not ready for that automation path. If most of the workflow can move, a pilot may be worth considering. If everything must stay local, you are looking at a self-hosted or tightly integrated approach. Less glamorous than a launch video, but more useful on Monday.
